in_kind_convention: MONETARY-ONLY AND MONETARY-PLUS-IN-KIND ARE IDENTICAL, tested both ways: NO row on either ledger is marked in kind (unlike this filer's October filing, where two rows were explicitly labelled 'In kind'), and the filing prints no in-kind line or column anywhere. Both conventions therefore give 17,475.00 on the contribution side and 27,618.35 on the expenditure side, and both close exactly. The one row that might tempt an in-kind reading - expenditure row 19, 'Bill Freeze / Reimbursement for FaceBook / 1,990.46' - is on the EXPENDITURE ledger, inside the range that closes to the cent, so it is a reimbursement paid out and not a contribution received.
escalation_note: No cell was doubtful: both ledgers are clean typed sheets and the cover is bold handwriting. The six 900 dpi crops taken are the mandatory geometry controls recorded in the frames. The one genuinely illegible cell on the filing - line 1 Column B, the cumulative contributions figure, which the filer over-wrote - was NOT escalated because it is a cumulative cell that this per-period regime never uses as an anchor; it is left honestly unread rather than guessed.
